kind: offline static evidence; no runtime validation or camera access

frame_descriptor.type_note: Video mux treats type 1 as random-access/sync sample; ordinary audio path writes 8 and EOS writes 0xff. Other enum values are not recovered.
frame_descriptor.timestamp_note: Both producers copy 64-bit source PTS. Common clock origin, units and DTS generation are not established by these observations.

virtual_fifo_creation.native_mp4_start: A01F6340 creates four virtual FIFO handles via A04509DC; each call passes capacity 0x2000 descriptors and virtual flag 1. Video and audio stream IDs are loaded from DAT_A13C82D8 and DAT_A13C7D20.
virtual_fifo_creation.existing_side_consumer_candidate: A0233508 (UVCd FIFO start) uses the same A04509DC ABI for stream DAT_A13C82D8, capacity 0x2000 and virtual flag 1, with callback DAT_A0233434; A0232E90 peeks index 0 and removes one entry, while A02335D0 deletes the handle.
virtual_fifo_creation.creator_abi_observed_fields: The first config words are stream_id (+0x00), capacity (+0x04), virtual (+0x08), and required callback (+0x0c). A04509DC also reads additional zero/default fields from the 0x58-byte config; their semantics are not recovered.
virtual_fifo_creation.base_link: A04509DC finds a base FIFO by stream ID and stores the base object link in the virtual handler; payload bytes are not copied during SyncWritten.
virtual_fifo_creation.filter_note: The handler contains a type/filter byte at +0xC0. The exact wildcard/filter initialization semantics are not assumed by the host prototype.

payload_ownership.encoder_ring: H264 setup receives bits FIFO base/limit; video events supply payload address (+0x14) and size (+0x18).
payload_ownership.fifo_behavior: AmpFifo_WriteEntry copies only the 0x20-byte descriptor into descriptor storage. AmpFifo_SyncWritten copies descriptors from base to virtual queues, not payload bytes.
payload_ownership.reclaim: Base FIFO reclamation considers virtual read cursors and payload address distance; a lagging virtual reader can constrain reclamation. RemoveEntry advances only the calling FIFO cursor.
payload_ownership.host_rule: Copy payload bytes before advancing the side reader; do not free or reuse firmware ring addresses and do not advance base cursor.

pts_path.descriptor_to_mux: A042CE28 calls A03E5B5C (AmpFormat_ConvertPTS) with descriptor PTS at +0x08/+0x0c.
pts_path.conversion: A03E5B5C uses mux stream state/timebase fields and writes converted PTS/DTS state; H264 setup exposes pts_delta at config offset +0x60.
pts_path.unknown: The static image does not establish the source clock epoch, exact unit selection for every mode, or a safe host-side DTS reconstruction rule.

close_lifecycle.normal_mp4: A01F6088 waits for mux completion, deletes mux resources, stops associated pipe/file objects, then deletes virtual FIFO handles with A04514E4.
close_lifecycle.event_mp4: A01F8F08 unregisters the EventRecord descriptor, waits/deletes mux resources, stops pipe/file objects, then deletes virtual FIFOs.
close_lifecycle.safety: This ordering is static evidence for the stock lifecycle only; a new side consumer must stop before its virtual FIFO is deleted and must not assume callbacks are quiescent without a runtime barrier.

limits: No proof of firmware injection, standby encoding or writable runtime hook.
An independent virtual FIFO has its own descriptor queue/read cursor; payload bytes remain shared in the encoder ring.
Slow side consumers can constrain base FIFO reclamation; copy payload promptly, then remove only own entries.
Native mux lifecycle exists but a second concurrent MP4 writer and seamless rollover are not runtime tested.
The UVCd callback/consumer is an existing static example of the creator ABI, not proof that an arbitrary new consumer can safely share the encoder ring without lifecycle synchronization.
